title: The Firehouse Chili Cook-Off
blurb: The volunteer fire department holds a chili cook-off every fall, and the judging has never once ended quietly.

text.intro:
The volunteer fire department holds a chili cook-off every fall, and the judging has never once ended quietly.
Six cooks are involved. Determine each cook's placing, chili, secret and topping.
- **Cook**: Bobbi Jo, Hollis, Sunny Deel, Luis Ortega, Verna and Gracie Mapp.
- **Placing** (listed from better to worse): first, second, third, fourth, fifth and sixth.
- **Chili**: a smoky chipotle chili, a plain old beef chili, a brisket chili, a green chile stew, a white chicken chili and a five-bean chili.
- **Secret**: a splash of cider vinegar, fire-roasted corn, cinnamon, a square of dark chocolate, nothing but salt and cold coffee.
- **Topping**: oyster crackers, shredded cheddar, crushed corn chips, a fried egg, scallions and sour cream.
Every cook has a different placing, chili, secret and topping, so within each category every item is used exactly once.
clues: The cook who enters a plain old beef chili is better than sixth in placing order.
The cook who swears by cold coffee is worse than fifth in placing order.

If (a) holds then (b) also holds, but not necessarily the reverse: (a) Gracie Mapp and first are exactly one place apart in placing order, in one direction or the other. (b) Bobbi Jo and the cook who swears by a splash of cider vinegar are exactly one place apart in placing order, in one direction or the other.
The cook who enters a white chicken chili falls somewhere between fourth and the cook who tops it with shredded cheddar in placing order.
Bobbi Jo and third are exactly one place apart in placing order, in one direction or the other.

The following two do NOT both hold; either one alone may hold, and so may neither: (a) The cook who tops it with sour cream is exactly one place better than fifth, with no placing in between. (b) The cook who tops it with a fried egg does not place fifth.
The cook who tops it with scallions and second are exactly one place apart in placing order, in one direction or the other.
The cook who enters a brisket chili is better than the cook who swears by a square of dark chocolate in placing order.
Hollis falls somewhere between the cook who swears by nothing but salt and the cook who tops it with scallions in placing order.
The cook who enters a brisket chili is better than the cook who tops it with oyster crackers in placing order.
Gracie Mapp is exactly one place better than the cook who tops it with sour cream, with no placing in between.
The cook who enters a brisket chili falls somewhere between Sunny Deel and Verna in placing order.
Hollis and the cook who swears by a splash of cider vinegar both sit at odd-numbered places or both at even-numbered places.
The following is NOT true: Sunny Deel is better than the cook who enters a smoky chipotle chili in placing order.
At least one of the following holds, and possibly more than one: (a) Hollis enters a plain old beef chili. (b) Bobbi Jo swears by a square of dark chocolate.

At least one of the following holds, and possibly more than one: (a) Gracie Mapp is better than the cook who enters a green chile stew in placing order. (b) Sunny Deel is better than the cook who enters a white chicken chili in placing order.
The cook who swears by cinnamon does not top it with a fried egg.
The cook who enters a green chile stew falls somewhere between the cook who swears by cold coffee and the cook who tops it with scallions in placing order.
The cook who swears by cinnamon falls somewhere between the cook who enters a brisket chili and the cook who enters a smoky chipotle chili in placing order.
The cook who enters a five-bean chili and Gracie Mapp are exactly one place apart in placing order, in one direction or the other.
The cook who tops it with oyster crackers falls somewhere between Sunny Deel and Verna in placing order.

At least one of the following holds, and possibly more than one: (a) The cook who enters a green chile stew and the cook who tops it with oyster crackers are exactly one place apart in placing order, in one direction or the other. (b) Hollis is exactly one place better than the cook who tops it with oyster crackers, with no placing in between.
